51372554.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human PD-L1 by surface plasmon resonance

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: ITC, SPR, and CD Analysis. All the proteins were obtained from Sino Biological if not otherwise specified (human PD-L1 (cat no: 10084-HNAH) and murine PD-L1 (cat no: 50010-M08H). SPR measurements were performed with PlexArray HT (Plexera Bioscience, Seattle, WA, USA). Briefly, human/murine PD-L1 was diluted to a final concentration of 0.25 mg/mL with sterile water or PBS and printed onto the bare gold-coated PlexArray Nanocapture Sensor Chip, and then P18 at different concentrations was injected by a nonpulsatile piston pump into the 30 μL flow cell, which was mounted on the coupling prism. The ITC experiment was performed using a MicroCal PEAQ-ITC (Malvern Panalytical Ltd., UK) according to the manufacturer’s guidelines. CD spectra were recorded on a Chirascan plus ACD (Applied Photophysics Ltd, England). Briefly, human/murine PD-L1 were incubated with sterile water or P18 at 25 °C for 30 min, and the CD wave scans were measured from 180 to 260 nm at 4 °C with a bandwidth of 2 nm and a step size of 1 nm.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. Real-time interaction between human PD-L1 and compound P18 (A) and murine PD-L1 and compound P18 (B).
original_paragraph.Results section: The high binding affinity of compound P18 to human or murine PD-L1 was further confirmed by the SPR experiment. As shown in Figure 4, P18 dose dependently binds to human PD-L1 and murine PD-L1 with K_D values of 202 nM and 471 nM, respectively, which is consistent with the ITC results.
